human_tolerance.notes: Terrestrial lizard of arid and semi-arid shrub-scrub with bare ground and low cover.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: Spring to summer breeding; seasonal dates vary by population.

taxonomy.note: Both providers independently resolve the accepted species name at species rank.

range.note: Account identifies a native Nearctic range extending through the western United States and central Mexico; country codes US and MX.

traits.note: ADW Physical Description gives typical mass 5.6-14.2 g and typical total length 38-89 mm, with adults rarely over 60 mm. Mass and length are midpoints of those typical ranges, converted to kg and m. 130 mm is a separate maximum and is not used.

traits.lifespan_y.note: For southern US and northern Mexico, the CC BY paper says lifespan is up to two years but usually one or less. Use 1 year as the rounded typical value for MX, retaining the published range and qualifier.

traits.diet.note: Generalist carnivore eats arthropods and occasionally small lizards; 95/5 allocation is an authored estimate.

traits.social.note: Usually solitary except during mating; group size is one as a simplified simulation representation.

traits.activity_pattern.note: Behavior section describes diurnal and crepuscular activity, most active in morning or late afternoon; mapped to Diurnal.

traits.defense.note: Seeks cover under rocks and shrubs when not basking, foraging or mating; tail autotomy is also described.

traits.wariness.note: Authored judgement for a small prey lizard that shelters from predators.

habitat.note: Terrestrial arid/semi-arid shrub scrub; proportions, resource weights and human tolerance are simulation estimates from the habitat and diet descriptions.

seasonal.note: Breeding begins April or May; the MX phase is an approximate spring-summer summary. Other populations differ and this does not set behaviour months.

activity.note: Generated from licensed observation histogram sources.

behavior.note: Species-local program models reported daytime/crepuscular foraging, warm-weather inactivity, and shelter under rocks or shrubs. Thresholds are authored simulation parameters.

vocalizations.note: No species call is included because the checked account does not document one.

look.note: Ground lizard proportions and neutral female/juvenile palette are authored; ADW describes grey/brown stripes, male blue/orange patches and colored throats. A single palette cannot represent sexual and geographic color variation.
